title: Critical Ising Model on the Periodic Cubic Lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$
abstract: We investigate the critical behaviour of the nearest-neighbour Ising model on the three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$, and we present a companion set of Monte Carlo simulations. After recalling the rigorous results on the continuity of the spontaneous magnetization in $d=3$ and the triviality of the scaling limit in $d\ge 4$, we compile modern high-precision estimates of the 3D Ising critical exponents and verify the scaling relations that connect them. We then describe numerical measurements of the Binder cumulant, the magnetic susceptibility, the specific heat, the two-point correlation function, and the finite-size scaling of the magnetization. We discuss the systematic uncertainties that affect the extraction of the exponent ratios $γ/ν$ and $α/ν$, and we emphasize that an exponential fit of the correlation function is not appropriate at the critical point, where the decay is algebraic.
summary: This paper performs a high-precision numerical investigation into the critical behavior of the 3D Ising model on a periodic lattice. By simulating various thermodynamic observables and applying finite-size scaling, the authors estimate the critical exponents and confirm the system's adherence to the 3D Ising universality class. It serves as a detailed computational benchmark for understanding classical phase transitions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the critical behavior and estimates the critical exponents for the nearest-neighbor Ising model on the three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice.
main_result: The study compiles high-precision estimates of the 3D Ising critical exponents and verifies the fundamental scaling relations connecting them, confirming the system belongs to the 3D Ising universality class.
method: The research combines theoretical analysis of known critical phenomena with extensive Monte Carlo simulations, employing advanced techniques like the Wolff algorithm and finite-size scaling (FSS).
model_or_system: The system is the Ising model with spins $\sigma_x \in \{+1, -1\}$ defined on a 3D periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$, governed by the Hamiltonian $H_{\Lambda,h}(\sigma) = -\sum_{\langle xy angle_{	ext{per}}} J \sigma_x\sigma_y - h \sum_{x \in \Lambda} \sigma_x$.
key_observables: Magnetization ($m$), specific heat ($C$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), Binder cumulant ($U_4$), and the two-point correlation function ($G(r)$).
important_parameters: The critical coupling $K_c = J/(k_B T_c)$ and the lattice size $L$ are key parameters; the analysis focuses on the critical point $T=T_c$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system belongs to the 3D Ising universality class and notes that exponential fitting of the correlation function is inappropriate at the critical point, where decay is algebraic.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of observables ($|m|, e, C_V, \chi$) for small lattices, and show data collapse plots for magnetization and specific heat using finite-size scaling.
paper_structure: The paper reviews known results for 2D and $d\ge 4$ lattices before focusing on $d=3$. It details the Monte Carlo simulations, presents measurements of various critical observables, and concludes by compiling the high-precision estimates and verifying scaling laws.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous study of critical exponents and universality classes provides foundational mathematical tools applicable to quantum phase transitions and critical phenomena in quantum many-body systems.
